chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both): In

If a man dies while his wife is under his guardianship but he has not yet consummated the marriage with her, he said: 'She is entitled to half of the dowry, and she inherits fully, and upon her is the complete waiting period.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a wife if her husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of a *mu'allaqah* (betrothed but not yet consummated) wife upon her husband's death, establishing that she retains full inheritance rights and observes the complete four-month ten-day waiting period. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes her status from a woman who was merely contracted but not yet in the husband's possession, ensuring she is treated as a full heir despite the lack of physical intimacy.
